title: Territories: shared/data.yaml
description: The Territories document (ie.napkin.territories). One schema for the engine, the app and the host; docs/contracts/territories.md says who writes and reads each member. Additive only: a new member is optional, a member is never removed or retyped (schema.lock.json fails the test).

schema_version.description: Bumped only for a breaking change, which the additive rule forbids until v2.

upstream.description: Frozen sources keyed by source document id (a brief, a research). Written by the host's spin-off; read-only for the app and the engine.

projection.description: The pins, findings and sources the carried research brought, as the host reads them (built at spin-off from the merged members, like every document that carries research). Host-written and read-only: the app counts from it, the engine reads the members themselves.

crew.description: At most 8 headings (5 default, the planner's own, one added).

territories.description: At most 32 routes: 8 headings x 4 routes.

id_insight.description: An insight on the Pick screen. Minted by the engine: in_ + 2-12 lowercase letters or digits.

id_crew.description: A crew member (agent with a heading).

id_expedition.description: One crew member's trail in one run.

id_check.description: One check on a developed route.

id_ask.description: A question the Booth puts to a person.

id_action.description: An action the engine took by itself, which has Undo.

id_lookup.description: A look-up (query to the research port).

id_note.description: A note on the record, from an agent.

id_send.description: One send to Deck Studio or the production tool.

id_picture.description: A picture slot on a route.

id_find.description: The tool's own find (a look-up result a person kept). Same shape as a pin id: x_ + 6 or more A-Z0-9.

cite.description: How a claim names its source. brief:<field> reads data.upstream.<brief doc id>.<field>; f_ and fi_ read the carried facts and findings members; x_ reads data.finds. Never copy a value; cite.

strength.description: Evidence strength shown on an insight; ranking is by this, then by number of cites.

band.description: Measured distance from the brief (shown to people as Core / Stretch / Far out). A route's band must match its distance by x-edges: core below 0.35, stretch below 0.65, far_out from 0.65.

tier.description: Judged risk (engine/territory/ladder.py TIERS). Stored, not shown by default.

direction.description: The crew's headings: close to the core, towards a feeling, the opposite pole, next door, far outside, the planner's own, one the planner added.

territory_state.description: found = a route with a thought; developed = it has its world, checks and marks.

origin_kind.description: Where a route came from: a crew member, a steer (go further / pull back), a cross of two, or the planner.

scene.description: Palette-sketch scenes drawn in v1. New scenes are added here.

font.description: Only the licensed faces (licences/fonts.toml) until the owner approves more.

by.description: A person's name, or `engine` for work the engine did itself.

inputs.description: What the person was looking at when they said yes: a short hash of the inputs of this gate (engine/territory/gates.py inputs_hash). An approval or review counts only while it equals the current hash, so one given for other inputs never passes this gate.

decision_in_doc.description: A person's approve / edit / retry at a gate.

kind.description: found = read by a look-up; case = from the case library

quote_checked.description: True only when the quote was checked against the page. Only checked quotes can be pinned.

find.description: The tool's own find, kept by a person. Separate from research pins; never written back to Research.

source_play.description: Whether a brief field, pin, finding or find is in play. By id only: no value is copied.

by.description: A person's name, or `engine` for work the engine did itself.

derived.description: True when it rests on a derived (unverified) finding.

insight.description: One insight the crew may explore.

waypoint.description: What a crew member picked up, and how far along its trail.

route_ref.description: A route a trail ended in, by distance from the brief.

by.description: A person's name, or `engine` for work the engine did itself.

steer.description: A person's instruction to a crew member.

heading.description: The brief this agent was sent out with, in words.

angle.description: Compass bearing; the planner never sees the number.

crew_member.description: An agent sent out on a heading.

expedition.description: One crew member's trail in this run.

palette.description: A territory's four colours. Ink on bg must be at least 4.5:1 (checked by territory.contract.check).

headlines.description: The headline for each corner of the tone x energy dial: wry-quiet, wry-loud, sincere-quiet, sincere-loud.

lead.description: A line a person led with; overrides the dial.

world.description: The campaign world a route opens as. Only this block is read by the touchpoint templates.

check.description: A check of a developed route against the brief, landscape, evidence and the blind judge.

marks.description: The three chips shown at greenlight.

blind.description: develop's blind /35 score (engine/territory/ladder.py). Stored; the person sees only the rank.

proof_case.description: A precedent case (IPA only in v1).

image.description: Path or asset ref of a frame.

sha256.description: Content hash of a frame: pick inputs by identity, never by eye.

gap_reason.description: Why there is no picture, in words.

picture.description: A picture slot. v1 draws palette sketches; frames come with territories-pictures-frames.

rank.description: The blind judge's order, shown instead of the /35 score.

territory.description: A route. Superset of Deck Maker's stage-d card: id, name, thought, why, mood, references, risks, sketch.

by.description: A person's name, or `engine` for work the engine did itself.

rests_on_derived.description: Derived findings this route rests on.

greenlit.description: A route a person greenlit. Blocked while rests_on_derived is non-empty and derived_resolution is pending.

by.description: A person's name, or `engine` for work the engine did itself.

ask.description: A question the Booth asks a person. Asked only for derived evidence at greenlight, near a mandatory, or a sensitive review.

undone_by.description: A person's name, or `engine` for work the engine did itself.

action.description: Something the engine did by itself. Always has Undo.

lookup.description: A look-up through the research port. No price here: counts only (run.calls).

note.description: A note on the record, shown in the Booth.

journey.description: One stop on the weekend journey; project-level, later fed from the media plan.

close.description: Pairs of routes closer than the threshold.

by.description: A person's name, or `engine` for work the engine did itself.

send.description: A hand-off. Routes not chosen travel too. production-tool reads `not_built` until production-spinoff merges.

by.description: A person's name, or `engine` for work the engine did itself.

inputs.description: What the person was looking at when they said yes: a short hash of the inputs of this gate (engine/territory/gates.py inputs_hash). An approval or review counts only while it equals the current hash, so one given for other inputs never passes this gate.

blocked_by.description: Why a gate cannot be passed yet, in words.

gate.description: The open gate. Nothing past it runs until a person approves.

calls.description: Counts only. Prices live in the decision history, never here.

message.description: In words a person can read: never a field name or a raw status.

refused.description: What the host refused, in words.

run.description: Mirrors deck-maker's run block so gates behave the same. No cost member: costs are for the Napkin team only.

by.description: A person's name, or `engine` for work the engine did itself.

inputs.description: What the person was looking at when they said yes: a short hash of the inputs of this gate (engine/territory/gates.py inputs_hash). An approval or review counts only while it equals the current hash, so one given for other inputs never passes this gate.

sensitive.description: Safe-messaging categories need a person's review before greenlit routes are sent.

focus.description: Step 1: what the crew may use, and what it will explore.
